title: Boss: incident on the web server
summary: Investigate a break-in from the logs, block it at the firewall, and harden SSH so it can't happen again.

steps.title: The incident
body: Monitoring flagged the web server. You have its `auth.log` lines, the router's FORWARD rules and the server's `sshd_config`. Work the incident loop: scope, contain, fix.

steps.title: Who got in?
prompt: Write `List<string> Compromised(List<string> authLines, int minFailures)` returning `"{user} from {ip}"` for each `Accepted password for USER from IP` line
where that IP had **at least** `minFailures` `Failed password` lines **earlier** in the log. Keep log order; report each user/IP pair once.
Failure lines look like `... Failed password for [invalid user ]NAME from IP port ...`.
template: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) dojoA.Add($"Nov 20 15:02:1{i} web sshd[1]: Failed password for invalid user admin{i} from 185.12.3.4 port 5123{i} ssh2");
dojoA.Add("Nov 20 15:03:00 web sshd[2]: Failed password for backup from 185.12.3.4 port 50000 ssh2");
dojoA.Add("Nov 20 15:04:40 web sshd[3]: Accepted password for backup from 185.12.3.4 port 50001 ssh2");
dojoA.Add("Nov 20 15:05:00 web sshd[4]: Accepted publickey for alice from 10.20.1.5 port 40000 ssh2");
dojoA.Add("Nov 20 15:06:00 web sshd[5]: Failed password for bob from 10.20.1.7 port 40001 ssh2");
dojoA.Add("Nov 20 15:06:10 web sshd[6]: Accepted password for bob from 10.20.1.7 port 40002 ssh2");
Dojo.Eq("brute force success", new List<string> { "backup from 185.12.3.4" }, Compromised(dojoA, 5));
Dojo.Eq("lower threshold also finds a typo", new List<string> { "backup from 185.12.3.4", "bob from 10.20.1.7" }, Compromised(dojoA, 1));
hints: Find the word `from`; the IP follows it and the user precedes it.
Count failures per IP as you go, so only *earlier* failures count.

steps.title: Contain at the firewall
prompt: Write `List<string> BlockRules(List<string> ips)` returning, for each distinct IP in order, the iptables command that inserts a drop at the **top** of FORWARD:
`iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s {ip} -j DROP`. Then, using the `Decide` evaluator from the firewall lesson (paste it with `ToUInt`), write
`bool Blocked(List<string> rules, string ip)` that is true when a new tcp connection from `ip` to `10.16.2.10:22` is dropped by `rules` with policy ACCEPT.
Note an inserted rule at position 1 goes **before** existing rules.
solution: if (!int.TryParse(p, out int n) || n < 0 || n > 255) throw new FormatException("bad octet " + p);
string Decide(List<string> rules, string policy, string src, string dst, string proto, int dport, bool established)
List<string> BlockRules(List<string> ips) => ips.Distinct().Select(ip => $"iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s {ip} -j DROP").ToList();
bool Blocked(List<string> rules, string ip) => Decide(rules, "ACCEPT", ip, "10.16.2.10", "tcp", 22, false) == "DROP";
template: Dojo.Eq("commands", new List<string> { "iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s 185.12.3.4 -j DROP", "iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s 6.6.6.6 -j DROP" }, BlockRules(new List<string> { "185.12.3.4", "6.6.6.6", "185.12.3.4" }));
var dojoRules = new List<string> { "-s 185.12.3.4 -j DROP", "-p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT" };
Dojo.Eq("drop after accept is too late", false, Blocked(new List<string> { "-p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT", "-s 185.12.3.4 -j DROP" }, "185.12.3.4"));
hints: `Blocked` is one call to `Decide` with policy ACCEPT.

steps.title: Fix the root cause
prompt: Write `string Harden(string config, List<string> admins)` that returns a new sshd_config: every existing line for `PasswordAuthentication`, `PermitRootLogin` or `AllowUsers`
(case-insensitive keyword, comments untouched) is removed, all other lines kept in order, and these three lines are **prepended** (first value wins, so they must come first):
Join lines with `\n`. Your `Audit` from the SSH lesson should report nothing for the result (the tests check that).
solution: var head = new List<string> { "PasswordAuthentication no", "PermitRootLogin no", "AllowUsers " + string.Join(" ", admins) };
template:
var dojoH = Harden("Port 22
PermitRootLogin yes
# PasswordAuthentication yes
passwordauthentication yes
X11Forwarding no", new List<string> { "alice", "bob" });

Dojo.Eq("result", "PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
AllowUsers alice bob
Port 22
# PasswordAuthentication yes
X11Forwarding no", dojoH);
Dojo.Eq("audit is clean", new List<string>(), Audit(dojoH));
hints: Filter lines whose first word (lowercased) is one of the three keywords; keep comments.
Prepend the three hardened lines and join with `\n`.
